chat: Doctor: Could you tell me more about how the gait and limb ataxia developed—was it sudden or gradual, and has it been worsening over time? Have you experienced any recent falls or balance issues?

It started gradually over the past few months, and yes, I’ve had a couple of falls recently when trying to navigate uneven surfaces. The weakness in my right arm has also gotten a bit worse, especially when I try to lift something.

Doctor: Has the patient had any recent infections or illnesses before the onset of ataxia? Any history of neurological conditions, autoimmune diseases, or family history of movement disorders? Also, have there been any recent changes in vision, speech, or swallowing?

I haven’t had any recent infections, but I do have Crohn disease, which has been hard to control. No history of neurological conditions, and I don’t think it runs in my family. I haven’t noticed changes in vision, speech, or swallowing, though.

The patient says: "I've had a gradual onset of gait and limb ataxia over the past year, with occasional falls. No recent infections, but I have a family history of Parkinson's disease. I’ve had some difficulty with speech clarity and mild memory issues lately."

Have there been any changes in mood, personality, or cognitive function, such as depression or anxiety? Has the ataxia been associated with tremors or muscle stiffness? Do you have any history of vitamin deficiencies, especially B12? I’ve been feeling more anxious lately, and sometimes I forget things more easily than before. The ataxia doesn’t seem to be accompanied by tremors or stiffness. I haven’t been tested for vitamin deficiencies, but I do have a poor appetite and have been losing some weight.
Doctor: Have you noticed any changes in coordination when performing fine motor tasks, like writing or buttoning clothes? Are there any episodes of dizziness, nausea, or vomiting?
I’ve had trouble with writing clearly, and buttoning clothes has become harder. I haven’t had dizziness, nausea, or vomiting, just more trouble with balance.
Has the patient experienced any episodes of numbness, tingling, or weakness in the arms or legs?
Not that I’ve noticed, but sometimes my right leg feels a bit weak when I stand for long periods.
The patient says: "No, no numbness or tingling, just the ataxia and occasional falls, plus some difficulty with speech clarity and mild memory issues."
Have you had any recent alcohol consumption or exposure to toxins? Have there been any episodes of confusion or hallucinations? Any history of head trauma?
I’m a social drinker, occasional weekend drinking, no toxins or head injuries.
Have you had any imaging or blood tests already?
No imaging yet, but I had some blood work recently; they said my B12 was normal.
Have you experienced any symptoms of anemia, fatigue, or weakness?
Not really, just the ataxia and occasional memory fogginess.
Have you noticed any urinary urgency or incontinence?
